intro.heading: Apply to CCC Church Residency.
intro.text: Everything happens in one online application, and your answers save on this device as you go, so you can finish in more than one sitting. Once you submit, a member of our residency leadership team will be in touch within a few business days about next steps.

fit.heading: Is this a fit?
points: You sense a call to explore vocational ministry
You have a bachelor's degree, or you want to complete thirty credit hours of Bible and theology through Crown College
You can commit to two years in Omaha (three on the counseling licensure track)
You have your own vehicle and transportation

steps.title: Gather a few things
steps.text: You'll need your church's info, your GPA, and names and emails for two leaders who know you.

steps.title: Fill out the application
steps.text: Tell us about yourself, your calling, your leadership, and what you believe. Your progress saves on this device as you go.

steps.title: Hear from us
steps.text: A member of our residency leadership team will reach out within a few business days about next steps.

application.heading: Application
application.text: Keep each written answer short, about 3–5 sentences. Fields marked with an asterisk are required.
application.saveNote: Your answers save on this device as you type. If you close this tab, come back on the same browser and pick up where you left off.

questionSteps.title: Your story
questionSteps.intro: Why the residency, and how God has been at work in your life.

questions.q: Why are you interested in becoming a resident at Christ Community Church?
What do you hope to take away from your residency experience?
What are the top 2–3 experiences you had while in college?
What are the top 2–3 lessons you learned in college outside of the classroom?
A big part of the residency is earning a master's degree through Crown College. Why do you think getting that degree is an important part of your leadership development?

questionSteps.title: Leadership
questionSteps.intro: How you lead, and who you learn from.

questions.q: Define leadership. Are you a leader? How do you know?
Describe your ministry leadership experience so far. What are the top 2–3 leadership lessons God has taught you?
What are your leadership strengths and weaknesses?
What leaders most inspire you? Why?

questionSteps.title: Beliefs
questionSteps.intro: In your own words. There's no need to look anything up.

questions.q: What do you believe about the authority of the Bible?
What do you believe about the triune God?
What do you believe about the doctrine of salvation?
What do you believe about the person of Jesus Christ?
What do you believe about the Christian life and the Holy Spirit?
What do you believe about human destiny?
What do you believe about the importance of being committed to a local church? Why?
What do you believe are the roles of men and women in church leadership?

statementOfFaith: There is one God, Creator of all things, who is infinitely perfect, existing eternally in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

Jesus Christ is the true God and true man. He was sent by the Father, conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin, Mary. He died upon the cross, the Just for the unjust, as a substitutionary sacrifice, and all who believe in Him are justified on the ground of His shed blood. He rose from the dead according to the Scriptures. He is now at the right hand of Majesty on high as our great High Priest. He will come again to establish His kingdom of righteousness and peace.
The Holy Spirit is a divine person, sent to indwell, guide, teach, gift, empower, and bear His fruit in every believer. He convicts the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgment.

The Old and New Testaments, inerrant as originally given, were verbally inspired by God and are a complete revelation of His will for our salvation. They constitute the divine and only rule of Christian faith and practice.

Man and woman, created in the image and likeness of God, fell through disobedience, incurring thereby both physical and spiritual death. Therefore, everyone is born with a sinful nature, is separated from the life of God, and can be saved only through the atoning work of the Lord Jesus Christ.

Salvation has been provided through Jesus Christ for all people. Those who repent and believe in Him are justified by grace through faith, born again of the Holy Spirit, delivered from the dominion of darkness, transferred into the Kingdom of God's Son, granted the gift of eternal life, and adopted as the children of God.

It is the will of God that each believer should be filled with the Holy Spirit and be sanctified wholly, being separated from sin and the world and fully dedicated to the will of God, thereby receiving power for holy living and effective service. This is both a crisis and a progressive experience wrought in the life of the believer subsequent to conversion.

Provision is made in the redemptive work of the Lord Jesus Christ for the healing of the whole person. Prayer for the sick and anointing with oil are taught in the Scriptures and are privileges for the Church in this present age.

The Church consists of all those who believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, are redeemed through His blood, and are born again of the Holy Spirit. Christ is the Head of the Body, the Church, which has been commissioned by Him to go into all the world making disciples of all peoples.

The local church is a body of believers in Christ who are called to love and joined together for the worship of God, edification through the Word of God, prayer, fellowship, proclamation of the gospel through word and deed, and observance of the ordinances of Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

There will be a bodily resurrection of all people. Our Lord Jesus Christ will judge with perfect justice as the unrepentant and unbelieving are raised to the conscious anguish of eternal separation from God, and repentant believers are raised to the unending joy of eternal life with God.

The Second Coming of the Lord Jesus Christ is imminent and will be personal, visible, and premillennial. This is the believer's blessed hope and is a vital truth which is an incentive to holy living and faithful service.

items.a: Two years. Residents on the Master of Arts in Counseling with state licensure track serve three years.
Residents raise their own monthly financial support, and CCC matches donations up to $400 a month per resident.

items.q: What does the master's degree cost?
items.a: Nothing. Your degree through Crown College is fully funded, including books and fees.
Yes. Coursework through Crown College is online, so you can complete it alongside your ministry work. Plan on 12–18 hours a week.
You can live with a CCC host family in a private room, with no rent or utilities. [Learn about host families](/host-families/).

items.q: Do I need a college degree?
items.a: No. Residents without a bachelor's degree complete the Crown 30 certificate, thirty credit hours of Bible and theology.

items.q: Can I choose my ministry area?
items.a: Yes. You'll choose a primary area of focus and work with a mentor in that area. [See the areas of focus](/program/#areas).
Yes. Residents provide their own vehicle and transportation.
